title: The longest and the shortest

lines: THE TIME IT TAKES TO TIE YOUR SHOES.
cards: Two surahs. One runs to two hundred and eighty-six verses, and reciting it aloud is an evening's work. The other you can say in the time it takes to tie your shoes, and a child can learn it in an afternoon.
They sit near opposite ends of the book, the second surah and the hundred and eighth, and Muslims hold that both are equally the word of God.

teach.b: The longest is al-Baqarah, the Cow, Surah 2. It's named for a story inside it: Musa telling his people to sacrifice a cow, and their endless questions stalling the command.
It holds a great deal: the story of Adam, the turning of the prayer toward Mecca, fasting in Ramadan, pilgrimage, charity, marriage and divorce, debts.

It holds the verse usually counted the longest in the Qur'an, about writing down a loan, and Ayat al-Kursi, the Throne Verse. Near its end, in Pickthall's words: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope."
The Prophet ﷺ said, in a hadith in Muslim: don't make your houses into graveyards; Satan flees from a house in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited. The shortest is al-Kawthar, Surah 108.
Al-'Asr and an-Nasr also have three verses, but al-Kawthar's three are the shortest of all. You met it in camp four. "Lo! We have given thee Abundance;" then: so pray to your Lord, and sacrifice.

Then: the one who hates you is the one cut off. Reports say it came at a hard time, when the Prophet's sons had died young and an enemy mocked him as cut off, a man with no line. Three verses to answer a grief.
A surah's weight isn't its length. Al-Kawthar is a whole surah, as complete as al-Baqarah. The Qur'an's challenge, made in al-Baqarah itself, is to bring a surah like it, and it names no length.
Both open with the same bismillah.

how: Many Muslims recite al-Baqarah at home, in portions or in full, because of the hadith about the house where it is recited, and al-Kawthar is among the short surahs often recited in the daily prayers.

o: the one who is left cut off

games.q: an enemy mocks you as 'cut off', a man with no sons to carry his name. what does al-Kawthar answer?
o: we have given you abundance; the one who hates you is cut off.
games.why: three verses: abundance given, pray and sacrifice, and the one who hates you is the one cut off.

practice: If you know al-Kawthar, say it now, slowly, all three verses, bismillah first; if you don't, remember it in English: abundance; pray and sacrifice; the one cut off.
Then stay with the first verse only, abundance, and let one thing you've been given but forget to count come to mind. If another comes, let it join the first.

wordCard.voice: Al-Kawthar. Abundance — the shortest surah in the Qur'an, just three verses, sitting opposite the two-hundred-eighty-six-verse al-Baqarah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: abundance, overflowing good. hadith also name al-Kawthar as a river in paradise.

carryVoice: Your line: long and short. Some days you need the whole house, and some days one room is enough. That's day three hundred twenty-five.
